name: Venice
shortDescription: The unfinished palazzo on the Grand Canal where Guggenheim's collection would eventually live.
description: Peggy Guggenheim bought the Palazzo Venier dei Leoni in 1949, a single-story palazzo left unfinished on the Grand Canal. She lived among her collection there for the rest of her life, opening the galleries and garden to the public every summer.

appearances.context: Guggenheim describes buying the unfinished palazzo and moving her collection in.

name: Cork Street, London
shortDescription: Site of Guggenheim Jeune, Peggy's first gallery, opened in 1938.
description: At 30 Cork Street, Guggenheim opened her first gallery, Guggenheim Jeune, with a Cocteau exhibition. It ran for eighteen months and lost money on nearly every show, but launched her as a serious presence in the art world.

appearances.context: The opening of her first gallery and the exhibitions that followed.
